constraints: No stored column value may change meaning; existing ledgers must still load
Display spellings shown to users must not change
The fix must fail at compile time or test time, not at runtime on a user's ledger
definition.objective: Several enums are persisted to SQLite by writing `as_str()` into a column and read back by deserializing that column through serde. This only works while a type's `as_str()` output and its serde discriminant agree, and for some policy enums they do not: `ProposalRecommendation::as_str()` yields "shadow-test" while its serde representation is "shadow_test", and `ApprovalRequirement` diverges the same way. Those two are not currently read back, so nothing is broken today — but the safety of the whole pattern rests on a coincidence that no test protects, and the next person to add a `WHERE recommendation = ?` filter or a parse of that column will not know. Make the round-trip a proved property rather than an accident: every enum whose value is written to a column and later parsed must be shown, by test, to survive the round trip, and any enum whose display spelling differs from its stored spelling must be structurally prevented from being read back by the generic parse path.

constraints: A configuration or naming error must not create a persisted run record
Existing successful run paths, including automatic routing, must behave identically
Error text must name the offending value and a concrete next command
definition.objective: `forge run` resolves the agent name before opening the ledger, but the pre-flight is uneven. An unknown agent id is rejected with a helpful message, yet the literal "auto" skips that check entirely, and an agent that appears in `[agents.<id>]` configuration but has no registered adapter is not caught until execution is already underway. The result is that a typo in a config section surfaces as a mid-run failure with a worse message than the same typo on the command line. Make the failure modes consistent: whatever a user can get wrong about agent selection should be reported before any workspace is provisioned, naming the specific problem and what to run to see valid options.

constraints: Re-recording an identical observation must remain safe and must not error
Recording a genuinely conflicting arm for the same run must not be silent
Existing experiment budget and reporting behaviour must not change
definition.objective: Phase 8 records which experiment arm a run landed on via `Store::record_experiment_observation`, which inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. That is correct for idempotent re-recording, but it makes two genuinely different situations indistinguishable to the caller: the observation was already recorded, or the insert matched nothing meaningful. The neighbouring `link_run_to_policy` was tightened to error when no run matched; this path was not. An experiment whose observations are silently dropped would still report a healthy status while its arms quietly diverge from the runs that actually happened. Make the outcome of recording an observation legible to the caller, and make it impossible to attach an observation to a run or an experiment that does not exist without an error saying so.

constraints: Warnings must never block a task that is merely unusual; validation and warning stay separate
No warning may fire for the existing `fixtures/test-repositories/median` task, which is correct
Do not execute or shell out to evaluator commands during validation
definition.objective: `EngineeringTask::warnings()` surfaces task-authoring mistakes at `forge task validate` time — a missing evaluation, missing protected paths, no constraints, a too-short objective. One common mistake is not covered: an evaluator that declares a `metrics_file` and is marked required, but whose command has no plausible way of producing that file. At runtime this does not fail loudly; the benchmark evaluator treats a missing or malformed metrics file as not-measurable, and the run lands as Inconclusive well after the agent has been paid for. Task authors should learn this at validate time. Extend the authoring warnings so a metrics-bearing evaluator whose contract cannot be satisfied is reported before the task is ever run, without producing false warnings for commands that legitimately write the file indirectly.

constraints: The unfiltered invocation must keep its current output exactly
Filter semantics must match `forge history`; two spellings of one concept is worse than none
The export schema version must change if and only if the record shape changes
definition.objective: `forge export --format jsonl` emits every run the ledger has ever held, with no way to narrow it. `forge history` already accepts a rich filter — agent, outcome, task, repository, experiment, date range, category, language, domain, difficulty, component, tag — and `HistoryFilter` is a public type in forge-store. Anyone analysing a single campaign, a single agent, or a single window currently has to export the whole ledger and filter it downstream, which gets slower and more error-prone as the ledger grows. Let export accept the same filtering vocabulary the history command already understands, so that the exported set is defined by Forge rather than by whatever the reader's script happened to do.

constraints: Historical runs that no policy governed must export as absent, never as a default or empty string
The change must be additive; existing consumers of schema version 1 must keep working
Bump the export schema version to reflect the new shape
definition.objective: `ExportRecord` is the analysis substrate: it carries the run, task revision, agent config, execution provenance, selection source, outcome, integrity, full evaluation, timings, usage, and patch stats. Phase 8 added three columns to `runs` — `policy_id`, `policy_fingerprint`, `policy_decision_id` — and the export does not include any of them. That means the exported record cannot answer which policy governed a run, so no offline analysis can compare outcomes across policies, which is precisely what the policy machinery exists to enable. Carry the policy linkage into the exported record, additively, so that a reader of an older export is unaffected and a reader of a new export can attribute every run to the policy that governed it or see explicitly that none did.

constraints: `Corrupt` must be left meaning what it says: an unreadable or hand-edited ledger
Every message must remain at least as specific as it is today
Callers that currently match on error kinds must keep compiling or be updated in the same change
definition.objective: `StoreError` is carefully typed for most of the ledger: rebinding a task revision, changing provenance, rewriting a finalized team execution, and conflicting artifact hashes each have their own variant with a specific message. The Phase 8 policy module does not follow that standard. It routes at least six structurally different failures — an invalid lifecycle transition, a fingerprint that no longer matches its record, a policy scoped to the wrong repository, a proposal filed with mismatched evidence, a decision misattributing behaviour to a policy — all through `StoreError::Corrupt`, a variant documented as meaning the ledger was written by something other than Forge or edited by hand. That is misleading: none of these indicate corruption, and a caller cannot distinguish "you asked for an illegal transition" from "your database is damaged". Bring the policy failures up to the standard the rest of the crate already sets.

constraints: Externally visible CLI behaviour, output, and error messages must not regress
Commands that legitimately need only the config, and not the ledger, must not be forced to open it
No new dependency between the CLI and crates it does not already use

complexity.command: files=$(ls crates/forge-cli/src/commands/*.rs | wc -l | tr -d ' '); opens=$(grep -c 'Store::open' crates/forge-cli/src/commands/*.rs | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END {print s+0}'); printf '{"metrics":{"cli_store_open_sites":{"value":%s,"unit":"sites","direction":"minimize"},"cli_command_modules":{"value":%s,"unit":"files","direction":"neutral"}}}' "$opens" "$files" > .forge-complexity.json

definition.objective: Almost every CLI command begins with the same four steps: discover the repository, build the layout, load the configuration, open the ledger at the configured path. `resolve_repository` is already shared, but each command module re-derives the store path and re-opens the ledger itself, and the error context attached to that open is duplicated in several places with slightly different wording. This is the seam where a new command is most likely to forget something — the health and policy commands each need the configured repository name, and getting it from the wrong place would scope a query to the wrong repository. Consolidate the repeated preamble into one place that hands a command everything it needs, so that adding a command cannot get the repository scope or the ledger path subtly wrong.

constraints: The optimizer must remain a pure function of supplied evidence; do not give it store access
Explicit user overrides must remain authoritative and must stay recorded as overrides
Historical runs must continue to carry no policy attribution
definition.objective: Phase 8's execution integration hands the caller a resolution describing which policy governs a task, and separately expects the caller to persist the resulting decision and link it to the run once the run id exists. Nothing in the type system requires the second half to happen. A caller that resolves a policy and forgets to persist the decision produces a run that silently looks like a Phase 0–7 execution — no policy attribution, no decision record — which is exactly the state the nullable columns are meant to represent honestly for historical runs. The gap between "no policy governed this" and "a policy governed this and we failed to write it down" is invisible after the fact. Make that contract harder to get wrong, so that resolving a policy and recording what it decided cannot drift apart.

constraints: Historical runs keep the harness they were recorded under; this is not a rewrite
An unknown agent must fail or be labelled deliberately, never silently mislabelled
The runner must not gain knowledge of specific agents beyond what the registry provides
definition.objective: Every run is recorded under a harness label — `claude-code`, `codex-cli` — and that label is how historical evidence stays interpretable after an agent is renamed or removed. The agent registry already carries the authoritative harness for each agent on its descriptor. The runner does not use it: it keeps a private lookup table mapping agent id to harness, with a fallback that quietly uses the agent id itself for anything it does not recognise. The two cannot disagree today only because both were written by hand. Adding an agent to the registry does not update the runner, so the first runs of any new agent would be recorded under a harness label that no descriptor claims, and nothing would report an error. Remove the second source of truth so a run's recorded harness cannot drift from the registry that defines it.

constraints: The test must exercise real concurrency against a real pooled connection, not a mocked sequence
It must be deterministic in its assertions and must not be flaky under load

definition.objective: Every durable id in Forge — runs, experiments, routing decisions, policies, proposals, decisions, health snapshots, world models — is allocated from a shared counters table, and the whole ledger's story depends on those ids never colliding and never being reused. The allocation is written as a single upsert-returning statement, which should be atomic, and the pool allows several connections. That property is currently asserted by nobody: there is no test in which concurrent writers race for ids and the result is checked. The cost of being wrong is silent and permanent — two runs sharing an id corrupts history in a way no later migration can repair. Establish the invariant as a test: under genuine concurrency, allocated ids must be unique, monotonic, and never reused after a failure or rollback.

definition.objective: Protected paths are the mechanism that stops an agent from editing the tests it is judged by. The whole evaluation-integrity guarantee reduces to whether a set of glob patterns matches the right files, and that matching is currently covered by a small number of illustrative cases. The interesting cases are the ones nobody wrote down: a pattern matching a directory versus its contents, nested double-star, a path that differs only by case on a case-insensitive filesystem, a file whose name contains glob metacharacters, a protected path that is also listed as an allowed exception, and a rename that moves a file into or out of the protected set. Strengthen the coverage of protected-path matching so that its behaviour on these cases is pinned by test rather than discovered during an incident.

definition.objective: Two of the ledger's widest read paths load evaluations one run at a time. `Store::export_records` iterates every run and issues a separate `load_evaluation` query per row; `health_run_evidence` does the same, with a comment acknowledging the choice and justifying it by the cost of reconstructing typed checks from a join. That justification is about parsing, not about round-trips, and the two are separable: the documents still have to be parsed once each, but they do not have to be fetched one query at a time. On a ledger with thousands of runs this is thousands of sequential round-trips for what is logically one scan, and both paths are on the critical path of `forge export` and `forge health build`. Reduce the round-trips without changing a single value either path returns.

definition.objective: `Store::policy_experiments` selects a page of experiment ids and then calls `policy_experiment_by_id` once per id, so listing twenty experiments costs twenty-one queries. The per-id method exists because status and conclusion time live in their own columns and must override what the stored JSON record says — a real requirement, since those are the two fields that move after an experiment is written. The listing needs the same override, which is why it was written this way, but it does not need a separate query to get it: the same columns are available in the page query that already ran. Collapse the listing to a single query while preserving the guarantee that the mutable columns, not the frozen JSON, decide an experiment's reported status.

definition.objective: `task_revision_profiles()` loads every task revision in the ledger, together with its components and tags, and builds a map of the whole corpus. Both `history()` and `export_records()` call it unconditionally on entry, before any filter is applied. A `forge history --limit 20` therefore materialises every task the repository has ever defined in order to annotate twenty rows, and the cost grows with the corpus rather than with the answer. The map is the right shape for export, which really does touch everything; it is the wrong shape for a filtered, limited history query. Make the cost of these paths proportional to the rows actually returned, without changing what either one returns.

constraints: Add a migration; do not edit an existing migration file
Evidence selection results and ordering must be unchanged, including tie-breaking
Existing ledgers must migrate cleanly and keep every historical row untouched
definition.objective: Phase 8's evidence path orders and filters runs by `COALESCE(finished_at, created_at)` — the instant a run's evidence actually became available, which is the correct key for reconstructing what was knowable at a historical cutoff. No index covers that expression. `runs_history_idx` covers `(created_at DESC, run_id DESC)` and cannot serve an ordering over a different expression, so every policy evidence resolution sorts the runs table from scratch, three times: once for the available window, once for the post-cutoff set, and once for the beyond-limit set. This is the query that runs every time a proposal is built or reproduced, and it is the one whose cost grows fastest with ledger size. Give the evidence-availability ordering index support, in a migration, without disturbing the existing indexes or the historical rows.

definition.objective: `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is the contract between Forge's ledger and every offline reader of it, and `ExportRecord` has already grown twice — execution provenance and selection source were both added as additive Phase 4 fields, each annotated in a comment explaining how older readers should treat them. Nothing verifies that promise. There is no test that a record written under an older schema version still deserializes, and no test that a newly added field is genuinely additive rather than breaking an existing consumer. The comments describe a compatibility policy that the code does not enforce, which is the state most likely to produce a silently broken export a year from now. Establish the compatibility guarantee as a test: pin representative serialized records for each schema version the format has had, and prove the current code still reads them and still writes something an older reader can consume.

constraints: Read-only; inspecting an experiment must not alter it or any run it links
Must not invent an overall winner where the recorded comparison declines to name one
A participant run that errored must still appear, marked as such, not omitted
definition.objective: `forge experiments list` shows recorded competitive experiments one line at a time, and that is the only way to see them. The ledger holds much more: each experiment records the base commit every participant shared, the agents that took part, the runs they produced, and a pairwise comparison with per-dimension relations that deliberately stops short of naming an overall winner. None of that is reachable without reading the SQLite file by hand, so the most interesting thing Forge records about a competition is also the least accessible. Give the experiments command a way to inspect a single recorded experiment in full, preserving the distinction the comparison itself makes between dimensions where one participant was better and dimensions where the evidence does not separate them.

constraints: Absolutely no agent execution, no workspace provisioning, and no run record
Must report the same resolution the real path would use, not a re-derived approximation
An explicit user agent choice must be shown as overriding what policy or routing would pick
Routing declining to select must be reported as such, not as an error

custom.command: before=$(cargo run --quiet --bin forge -- history --limit 1000 2>/dev/null | wc -l); cargo run --quiet --bin forge -- run .forge/tasks/example.yaml --help >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; after=$(cargo run --quiet --bin forge -- history --limit 1000 2>/dev/null | wc -l); test "$before" = "$after"

definition.objective: Starting a run is expensive and irreversible in the ways that matter: it provisions a worktree, spends real provider budget, and writes a permanent ledger record. Yet there is no way to find out what a run *would* do first. Which agent routing would pick, whether routing would decline to pick at all, which policy is in force and what it resolves to, how much repository context would be supplied, and which evaluators the task declares are all decided inside `forge run` and only become visible once the money is committed. Let a user see that resolution without executing anything, so a task can be checked against the strategy that will actually govern it before an agent is started.
